doc.title: Roland Hanna interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, April 15, 2000

chapter: Sarah Vaughan's band on the road
title: Writing charts for Sarah Vaughan's band in Reno
summary: Bobby Bryant and Gerry Wiggins helped; the twelve-piece band and the rhythm section; his tenure of 1960-63.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Did you get a chance to hear them before the gig?

Well at least I got a chance — Bobby Bryant, the trumpet player, a wonderful trumpet player, he was on the gig and he helped me a great deal. I managed to write about six charts and he wrote about three or four more. And when I got hung up writing them — you probably know Gerry Wiggins.

The pianist, a wonderful pianist. He let me have his apartment to do the writing. And then he came and helped me by doing some copying for me. Because those guys, I’ll never forget them because they were great at a time when I knew nothing.

That was — let’s see — four saxes, one trombone player, two trumpets. It was a small band, a twelve piece band probably. The rhythm section was me, Richard Davis and Percy Brice. And nine other guys. We had no guitar. But it had to be a nice band.
The time with Sarah was early 1960s?
